accounting.rationale: J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, PDF 75, printed 61, lines 4-5: the two subdivisions account for the abstract concept and its independence from a particular representation.
Type is the abstraction used to categorize data. This introduces terminology, not a new storage-format or executable oracle.

The abstraction does not identify a physical representation. Kind values, byte widths, IEEE encodings and native character codes must not be inferred from a type name. Processor-specific value sets remain governed by 7.1.3 and 7.4.
PDF 75 lines 6-7: four characteristics of a type, each separately accounted below.
A type has a name. Accessibility is a separate restriction in 7.1.2 p3, not evidence obtained by declaring an arbitrary object.
A type has a valid-value domain. 7.1.3 supplies the category-specific definitions; a handful of representable values cannot establish the domain.

A type has a means of denoting its values. Read with 7.1.4, 7.4, 7.5.10, 7.6 and 7.8, including their constant-expression conditions. This does not assign a type to BOZ literals, which 7.7 p1 explicitly makes typeless.

A type has operations for its values, with the empty intrinsic operation set for derived types preserved by 7.1.5 p2 and 7.5.11. This is not a promise of every operator for every category or kind. Operation availability and its pending use-graph evidence are recorded in the 7.1.5 catalogue.

review_rationale: Independent original-source review and verified gate repairs: doc/source_audits/batch_007.json. Type concepts receive source accounting without artificial runtime cases or a definition-only excuse to omit real obligations in the surrounding scopes.
